```{r, include = FALSE}
has_keys <- nzchar(Sys.getenv("EIA_API_KEY")) &&
  nzchar(Sys.getenv("BEA_API_KEY"))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(rpspanel.cache_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "rpspanel-vignette"))
```

`rpspanel` builds a documented, reproducible state-by-year panel for the 50
US states and DC. It combines EIA energy, electricity and CO2 data, BEA
GDP, income and population, and standardised Renewable Portfolio Standard
(RPS) stringency measures.

```{r setup}
library(rpspanel)
```

## API keys

EIA and BEA data need free API keys:

* EIA: <https://www.eia.gov/opendata/register.php>
* BEA: <https://apps.bea.gov/API/signup/>

Put them in your `.Renviron` file (open it with
`usethis::edit_r_environ()`), then restart R:

    EIA_API_KEY=your-eia-key
    BEA_API_KEY=your-bea-key

## One call, one panel

```{r panel, eval = has_keys}
panel <- build_panel(years = 2005:2022)
panel
```

Pick variables by group or by name. Derived variables fetch what they need:

```{r vars, eval = has_keys}
small <- build_panel(
  states = c("CA", "TX", "NY", "IA"),
  years  = 2010:2022,
  vars   = c("co2_pc", "re_share_nonhydro", "gdp_real_pc", "rps_nominal")
)
head(small)
```

If one source cannot be reached, its variables are left out with a warning
and the rest of the panel is still returned.

## Codebook and citations

Every variable has a definition, unit, source series and transformation:

```{r codebook}
head(codebook(), 10)
codebook(group = "rps")
```

`cite_sources()` lists the sources used, with the date each was retrieved:

```{r cite}
cite_sources(c("eia_seds", "eia_co2", "bea_regional"))
```

## Caching and vintages

Downloads are cached, so a panel can be rebuilt offline with exactly the same
data vintage. Use `refresh = TRUE` to download fresh data, `rps_cache_list()`
to see what is cached and `rps_cache_clear()` to empty the cache.

```{r cache}
rps_cache_dir()
```

## RPS measures without API keys

RPS stringency measures come from the coded rules bundled with the package,
so they work offline:

```{r rps}
rps <- build_panel(states = c("CA", "WA", "NC", "TX"), years = 2005:2025,
                   groups = "rps",
                   rps_methods = c("adoption", "nominal", "flexibility"))
rps[rps$year %in% c(2010, 2020), ]
```

See `vignette("rps-stringency")` for the methods.

## Estimation and export

The panel works directly with `plm`, `fixest` and `csdm`:

```{r estimate, eval = has_keys && requireNamespace("fixest", quietly = TRUE)}
library(fixest)
p <- build_panel(years = 2001:2022,
                 vars = c("co2_pc", "rps_nominal", "gdp_real_pc"))
feols(log(co2_pc) ~ rps_nominal + log(gdp_real_pc) | state + year,
      data = as_pdata(p, "fixest"), cluster = ~state)
```

Export to CSV, Stata or Parquet, with the codebook alongside:

```{r export}
f <- file.path(tempdir(), "rps_panel.dta")
if (requireNamespace("haven", quietly = TRUE)) export_panel(rps, f)
```
